column3: PROVISIONAL (india-24c, India-relevant): FAO 2019 (ca5644en.pdf) Table 1 Group 1 p.11 "Fresh, squeezed, chilled, frozen, or dried fruit and leafy and root vegetables"; exact term not named by the clause (an instance of the class 'fruit'; inference level: class-instance of fruit; the clause names 'fruit' without listing species, and the Group 1 definition names 'edible parts of plants (fruit, seeds, leaves, stems, roots, tubers)' (same table); botanical fruit used as vegetables or berries/drupes/pomes/tropical fruit are instances of the class, none is named); plain raw or frozen-unprepared form (inference level: class-instance). Identity (naming and use only, never placement): Morton, Fruits of warm climates (1987) via Purdue NewCROP, https://hort.purdue.edu/newcrop/morton/karanda.html, Carissa carandas: "called ... karaunda in Malaya and India; Bengal currant or Christ's thorn in South India"; "The sweeter types may be eaten raw out-of-hand but the more acid ones are best stewed with plenty of sugar." Pickle, jam, dried and powder forms follow the fruit rules (abstain or their own markers).

G. subinaequalis): "Phalsa is the most used vernacular name in India"; "only one genus, Grewia, yields edible fruit" in the family.
